verification.explanation:
The change delays building the filtered endpoint slice until a built-in read-only load-balancer actually drops an endpoint. In the steady state, it reuses the route slice; mixed-age filtering still returns an ordered copy, and the all-dropped fallback is unchanged. Because `LBAlgorithm` receives a mutable endpoint slice, unmarked custom algorithms keep the previous defensive copy. A public postprocessor test uses a custom algorithm that swaps endpoints; a diagnostic version with unconditional reuse failed that test, reversing the stored route order and changing the next selected backend. The change therefore follows the lazy-copy direction where the consumers are source-proven read-only, without changing the custom-algorithm contract.

The full-request benchmark fixture remains in proof support and is not shipped. It reaches `Proxy.ServeHTTP` with the default transport, access logging disabled, 200 distinct warmed local 204 backends, a one-hour fade-in, and endpoints aged two hours. The measured consumer metric is B/op: allocated bytes for each completed benchmark request iteration. In the prepared five-second runs, B/op fell from 38,976 to 25,406 for power-of-random choices, random, and round-robin, and from 39,008 to 25,438 for consistent hash; allocs/op also fell by one in each workload. The measurement system applies the declared bounds. Production traffic frequency for steady-state routes remains unmeasured and can be checked with production telemetry after deployment.

The shipped additions are behavior and regression tests, not benchmark-measurement machinery; the full-request benchmark stays outside the shipped change. Formatting and lint/build receipts passed, and two interleaved full TestFadeIn runs passed on both revisions. A broader package run was not wholly green: the final-only TestPHC counter failure used routes without fade-in and returned through the unchanged zero-duration branch; other failures were outside the modified path. Full repository CI remains pending.
